record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let p be a polynomial in two complex variables whose zero set p=0 is smooth, irreducible, and rational. Must p be a factor of a field generator, equivalently of a generically rational polynomial, so that there exists a polynomial q for which the generic fiber of pq is rational?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 3. If the polynomial p in two variables over C has smooth, irreducible rational zero set, is p a factor of a ﬁeld generator (or generically rational polyno mial), i.e. does there exist a polynomial q such that the generic ﬁbre of pq is rational ?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $p \in \mathbb{C}[x,y]$ be a polynomial in two variables over $\mathbb{C}$ whose zero locus $\{p=0\} \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ is smooth, irreducible, and rational (i.e., birational to $\mathbb{A}^1_{\mathbb{C}}$). A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[x,y]$ is called a field generator (equivalently, a generically rational polynomial) if there exists a rational function $g \in \mathbb{C}(x,y)$ such that $\mathbb{C}(f,g) = \mathbb{C}(x,y)$, or equivalently if the generic fiber of $f \colon \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ is a rational curve. Must $p$ be a factor of some field generator? Equivalently, does there exist a polynomial $q \in \mathbb{C}[x,y]$ such that the generic fiber of the product $pq$ is rational?
artifact.category_tag: field generators of polynomial rings in two variables
